reason: The cited evidence does not address dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy alloys or their interfaces. E1 discusses single-phase BCC creep, E2 describes shear banding and nano-twins at grain boundaries in a single-phase BCC alloy, and E3 only defines creep parameters. None of the key premises about heterogeneous phase boundaries are supported.
premises: FCC/BCC interfaces act as effective barriers to dislocation motion
Dislocation pile-up at interfaces creates internal back stresses
Pile-up triggers local nano-twinning near interfaces
This synergistic response delays creep compared to a homogeneous microstructure
